messages.subject: Env Data
parts:
Hi. I have problems loading my variable layers. When I click on Load Env Data an error appears informing that the raster do not have a defined system of coordinates. The raster are defined in WGS 84 UTM zone 20S.
Anyway, I tried to solve it following the steps of Module Guidance:
library(raster)
r <- raster(path_to_raster_file)
# an example for the common CRS called WGS84 (a latitude / longitude projection)
# the text format for these CRS's is called proj4
crs(r) <- crs("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs")
# save the raster with defined CRS to file
writeRaster(r, path_to_new_projected_raster_file)
This did not work for me, the coordinate reference keeps giving NA.
Could you help me?. Thank you.
Ailin

messages.author: d73691b565754184
messages.subject: Re: Env Data
parts:
Dear Ailin,

One problem that you have is that your localities are in a geografic coordinates system (GCS) and your raster is in a projected coordinate system (More info).
You need to convert your raster to a GCS. You can use the raster::projectRaster() funtion in R (More info) or the GIS of your preference (e.g., QGIS, ArcGIS).

r <- raster(path_of your_raster) 
# Define the Proj.4 spatial reference
sr <- "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"
# Project Raster projected_raster <- projectRaster(r, crs = sr)

Let me know if you need more help.

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.author: d73691b565754184
messages.subject: Re: Env Data
parts:
Hi Ailin,

I think that your machine specification is good enough to project your raster. I suggest to run the code in a "fresh" session in R. I just project your raster following the next code:

library(raster)
r <- raster(your_path_file)
crs(r) <- "+proj=utm +zone=20 +south +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"  # I assumed that the CRS of your original raster is WGS84 UTM 20

# Define the Proj.4 spatial reference
sr <- "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"
# Project Raster
projected_raster <- projectRaster(r, crs = sr)

writeRaster(r, filename = "name_for_the_projected_raster.tif")  # I suggest TIF files, but you can specificy ASC if you want.

Let me know if this works for you.

Best,
Gonzalo
